items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: The interviewer states: '...knew well that Davy Tuff and Krupa has played on many occasions with the Condon gang...' The interviewee does not contradict this or claim a personal relationship, merely narrating the context of the Chicago jazz scene.

ctx.x: We've talked about Chicago style without saying specifically how it was different from, well, just anybody's dance music. Because I think you and I seem to feel that it's so familiar we don't have to do that. But have you ever broken it down into elements and say where it's different, how it's different?

Well, I think we've already mentioned the fact that the force and drive is one of the most important aspects of it. It seems to me that it's easiest if you break it into instruments. That we associate it, for instance, with a tenor, clarinet, and trumpet. We don't associate it with piano. Because I don't think there was any particular... There were some exceptions, but generally it wasn't a particularly distinguished piano. With the exception of Steve Brown, who you don't really associate with Chicago…
Now, you wouldn't say that the riff was a characteristic of Chicago. It isn't quite that, is it?
